historical_references.reference: The Parmars were a Jain dynasty that ruled in Malwa, central India, from the 10th to the 13th century AD. The Parmar rulers are known for their patronage of Jainism and their role in preserving ancient Jain texts.

The Parmars were also known as the Paramaras, and one of their notable rulers was Bhoja (r. 1018-1063 AD). He is famous for his patronage of arts and learning, and is believed to have commissioned the construction of the temples at Mount Abu and the Bhojshala temple in Ujjain.
